thread:
Mira Patel: quick question — noticed confusing behavior when creating an experiment with sample_rate < 1 and per-variant quotas. Console preview shows expected split but production traffic seems to fall back to default more than we'd expect. anyone seen this?
Samir Khan: hm. is sample_rate applied before we evaluate quota guards, or after variant assignment?
Jon Ruiz: afaik current gateway flow: 1) check if request is in experiment (sampling) 2) evaluate routing guards/quota 3) assign variant. but maybe quota rejections trigger fallback outside the experiment path.
Lena Cho: that ordering sounds right, but we had a bug where quota checks were gated by "is_in_experiment" and then fallback logic used the partitioner for the full population. result: some users sampled out, others end up hitting default when variants are exhausted.
Mira Patel: here's the experiment payload I used in Console preview:
```json
{
  "name": "pricing_prompt_v2",
  "sample_rate": 0.2,
  "variants": [
    {"id": "control", "weight": 50, "quota": 10000},
    {"id": "treatment", "weight": 50, "quota": 2000}
  ],
  "guards": [{"type": "region", "allow": ["us","eu"]}]
}
```
Mira Patel: at 20% sample rate and treatment quota 2k, we expect ~0.2 * traffic to be eligible and then treatment to get ~50% of that — so ~10% of overall. but metrics show treatment is ~3% and default is 17% (default meaning not in experiment, not control).
Samir Khan: sounds like "quota_reject -> default fallback" is being counted against the experiment sample. i.e., sampled-in requests that hit a quota rejection are routed back to default path but still counted as sampled when you just look at the traffic slice. That will skew per-variant exposure.
Jon Ruiz: agree. Two ways to handle: 1) treat quota_exhausted as "not in experiment" (roll sampling back) so sample_rate guarantees still hold, 2) treat quota_exhausted as experiment-internal fallback (counts against sample). Both are defensible.
Lena Cho: for product expectations, customers assume sample_rate is end-to-end. i.e., if they set 20% they expect ~20% of users to see experiment vs not. If quota rejections secretly reduce visible experiment traffic, that's surprising.
Samir Khan: implementation cost: option 1 requires us to re-run sampling when a quota triggers (or to decrement a counter). That can cause re-hashing issues and small race windows. Option 2 is simpler (current) but we must show it in UI and telemetry.
Mira Patel: can we add a clear UI explanation and a preview number showing "effective exposure" after guards & quotas? E.g. show "expected sample: 20% — estimated after quotas: 12%" and a tooltip explaining fallback semantics.
Jon Ruiz: yes. Also need telemetry events so we can measure this precisely: propose: 
- experiment.assignment_attempt (sampled=true/false, sample_rate, assigned_variant)
- experiment.quota_reject (variant_id, reason)
- experiment.fallback (from_variant, to=default|alternate_variant)
- experiment.effective_exposure (daily aggregate)
Those let us compute both raw sample and post-quota exposure.
Lena Cho: add one more: experiment.preview_estimate when user edits experiment in Console (computed from historical traffic distribution + quotas).
Mira Patel: Dev question: should the router apply sample_rate before guard evaluation? If sample_rate is applied first then many requests won't even hit guard checks and won't count against quotas. That protects quotas but leads to quotas being underutilized.
Samir Khan: correct. If we sample first, quota is only consumed by the sampled cohort. That keeps quota predictable per-experiment but makes global guard checks less useful (e.g., region filter won't prevent sampling decisions for out-of-region users unless you check region earlier).
Jon Ruiz: nice summary: ordering tradeoffs: 
- Sample -> Guard -> Assign: quotas constrain only sampled users; cheaper but guards may be bypassed for logging/metrics.
- Guard -> Sample -> Assign: quotas apply post-guard; ensures only allowed users consume quota, but sample_rate acts on a smaller population so you need to clarify expected numbers.
Lena Cho: UX should let people pick a "guarding" mode? maybe a toggle: "Apply sample before guards" (default: guard->sample). But that adds complexity.
Mira Patel: for now i suggest we keep guard->sample by default (safer for compliance) and: 
- show an explicit "effective exposure" estimate in Console UI,
- emit the telemetry events Jon suggested,
- add a short line in the API docs about fallback behavior (quota_exhausted -> default route) and which order is used.
Samir Khan: +1. we should also add an integration test for a toy workload: simulate 1M requests with sample_rate 0.1 and variant quotas small, assert effective exposure within tolerance.
Jon Ruiz: i'll add unit tests in routing service and a canary integration in staging. Mira — can you add the UI copy and preview numbers? Lena — can you own the docs update? Samir — will take telemetry events.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for routing-service branch feat/experiment-quota-fix -> staging at 1729802600 :rocket:
QA: will run the integration sim once deploy is up. i'll post results here.
Mira Patel: thanks all — assigning tasks: Jon (routing tests & canary), Samir (telemetry), Lena (docs), Mira (console estimate + tooltip). i'll open a GH issue linking to this thread. :raised_hands:
